text:
Lena (Finance): Heads up 10K payment to vendor 'DataHarbor' on hold. They asked to gross-up payment because we applied 30% withholding due to missing W-8. They sent an email asking for gross-up and a delayed W-8-E.
VendorBot: Payment PH-2024-559 queued amount: $10,000 withholding applied: 30% ($3,000). File: payment_note.pdf
Marco Tax: Quick rules: we only gross-up if contractually agreed or company policy permits. Usually vendor must provide W-8BEN-E to claim treaty relief or no US withholding. If they send W-8 that proves foreign status, we can refund withholding but gross-up is exceptional.
Priya (Vendor Ops): Vendor says they are preparing W-8BEN-E and request the gross-up because they "can't afford the hit". No contract clause about gross-up. They offered to accept a net payment if we pay additional fee.
Lena (Finance): Our standard is no gross-up unless SOW or procurement approves. Can procurement escalate? Also need to validate taxpayer status and effective date on W-8.
Marco Tax: Ask vendor to submit completed W-8BEN-E immediately and provide a primary contact. If W-8 proves non-US status and no treaty benefits, we will refund the withheld amount on next payout (not gross-up). If contractually required, escalate to legal/procurement for approval.
Priya (Vendor Ops): Sending vendor copy: "Please send completed W-8BEN-E signed and dated, plus a corporate registration extract. We will review and, if valid, refund any withholding. Company policy doesn't permit unilateral gross-ups without prior approval"
Lena (Finance): Putting PH-2024-559 payment on hold. SLA to vendor: 3 business days to submit W-8 or we proceed with withholding. Logging in payment recovery tracker.
Marco Tax: If they push for gross-up, procurement/legal need to confirm commercial exception. I'll add a note in the tax binder.
Priya (Vendor Ops): Vendor acknowledged and will submit W-8 by EOD. I'll update once received.
Lena (Finance): Thanks. Will only release once W-8 validated and refund arranged if applicable. Closing after bank confirms adjustment.
